titulo: Product ads and UGC: the structures that work and the lines you don't cross
lead: UGC is the ad that looks like a video from an ordinary person: someone holds the product in their hand and talks to a phone camera. With AI you can make it without filming anything, and that is exactly where the risk lives: an invented testimonial passed off as real. This lesson teaches the structures and the rules that keep the ad honest.
objetivo: write a 15 to 30 s ad in five blocks, with a spoken line, the product in frame early, and a made-with-AI content label.

aprende.t: Choose an ad structure: review, confession, routine, first reaction
Build the 30 s skeleton in five blocks with spoken lines
Keep the product the same in every shot
Label it and don't cross the lines: real person, fake testimonial, false promise

hero_alt: A small tabletop set for filming a product: a smooth glass bottle on a white turntable, a softbox, a reflector and a phone on a mini tripod.

secoes.sub: Five blocks, with the timing of each. Tap each block.

nos.detalhe: Starts in the middle of a thought, with the product already entering the frame within the first three seconds. No still logo opening the video.
The person says what the product is and shows it to the camera. One sentence, the way you'd talk to a friend.
The product in use, in hand. It's the shot that convinces the most and the one most worth filming for real, if the product exists.
What changes after using it. Only what the product really delivers: an invented result is false advertising, with or without AI.
A light ending, with no aggressive selling. And the label: made with AI, fictional person when that's the case.

secoes.legenda: Skeleton and rules from the INEMA ugc-seedance25 skill (Sep/2026); the label is an addition of this course.

secoes.titulo: How to write the ad, step by step
secoes.sub: The example product is fictional: the sourdough bread from Dona Lia's bakery.

texto: Review: the person uses it and comments. Confession: problem, ritual, result. Routine: the product in everyday life. First reaction: open the box and react. 15 s selfie test: short hook, one benefit, casual ending.
Choose by product: the bread calls for routine (the morning of whoever buys it) or confession ("I gave up on supermarket bread").
Write the spoken line for each block in quotes, with the timing next to it. The INEMA skill uses 70 to 80 spoken words in 30 seconds: more than that, and the line gets rushed.
Sound: list what must not appear (loud music under the voice, for example). The look is phone-made: home lighting, no text on screen during generation.

Use the same reference photos of the product (one main one and two or three detail shots) in every generation, as course 1 teaches in the consistency lesson. Change one thing at a time and generate one before the batch.
The product's label and text go in during editing, not in the prompt: the generator tends to distort letters. Check every shot: only one product, the right hands, the same face.

A generated person is never presented as a real customer. A synthetic testimonial carries a label. The promised result is what the product delivers. A real person's face and voice, only with written permission.
No competitor brands and no famous people. The labeling law and the cases are in lesson 7; the platform where you advertise may have its own rules.

secoes.exemplo:
Product: Dona Lia's naturally leavened bread from her bakery (a fictional product made for the course)
Structure: confession (problem, ritual, result) · 9:16
Label: video made with AI; the customer is a fictional character
# n | block | time | what you see | line
1 | hook | 3 s | The bread enters the frame already torn in half, steam rising. | line: "I had given up on real bread."
2 | what it is | 6 s | She holds the bread up to the phone camera, in her kitchen at home. | line: "This is the naturally leavened one from the bakery on the corner."
3 | demonstration | 7 s | She cuts a slice; the crust crackles and the crumb opens up. | line: "Listen to that crust. It stays like this until the next day."
4 | result | 7 s | Breakfast on the table, the family reaching for slices. | line: "Now breakfast starts at 6:50 in line at the bakery."
5 | ending | 5 s | She takes a bite and smiles. | line: "The first batch comes out at 5. Go early."

exercicios.titulo: Ad · five blocks with a label
exercicios.texto: Choose a structure and write the Produto, Estrutura and Rótulo lines and the five blocks with time, what is seen and the line. Paste it into "Check your ad" and download the anuncio.txt to the project folder.
exercicios.pronto: the page answers OK: anúncio com [n] blocos, fala e rótulo · [s] s, with the total between 15 and 30 s, and the anuncio.txt is in the project folder.

exercicios.titulo: Promise · only what the product delivers
exercicios.texto: Read the result block and write, next to the anuncio.txt, a "Prova:" line saying where each promised thing comes from (does the product do that? who confirmed it?). Cut from the script whatever has no proof and check again.
exercicios.pronto: the page keeps answering OK: … and each promise in the result block has its own "Prova:" line in the file.

secoes.sub: Four questions. The explanation appears after each answer.

perguntas.p: At what moment should the product appear in the 30 s ad?
opcoes: Only at the ending, to build suspense until the end.
After the demonstration, once the person has talked about it.
In the first three seconds, right in the hook.
In no generated shot: only in the final label.
perguntas.explica: People scrolling decide in seconds. The product in the hook says right away what it is about; long suspense loses the audience before that.

perguntas.p: The product label came out with crooked letters in the generated shots. What should you do?
opcoes: Put the label and the product text in the edit, not in the prompt.
Ask in the prompt for the generator to write more carefully.
Make the label bigger in the prompt so it reads better.
Generate again until the text comes out right by chance.
perguntas.explica: Generators often warp letters. Text goes in post, on top of the shot; regenerating by luck burns credits.

perguntas.p: Which of these lines crosses the line?
opcoes: "This is the naturally leavened one from the bakery on the corner."
"The first batch comes out at 5 a.m. Come early."
"I've been a customer for ten years, and this bread cured my gastritis."
perguntas.explica: The person is fictional, so "a customer for ten years" is a fake testimonial, and the health claim has no proof. The other two describe the product without making anything up.

perguntas.p: Why does this course's script require the Label line?
opcoes: Because the video generator refuses a script without a label.
Because the label replaces permission to use the image and voice of the people who appear.
Because an ad with a generated person or testimonial has to tell viewers.
Because the label makes the ad shorter.
perguntas.explica: Viewers need to know the person and the scene were generated. A label is not a substitute for permission: real faces and voices still require consent (lesson 7).

itens.texto: Five blocks in 30 s, with the product in the first three seconds.
Locked reference, one change at a time, product text added in the edit.
A generated person is not a real customer; only promise what the product delivers.
